final_assessment: Archived single-chat-move to orbit/changes/archive/2026-10-17-single-chat-move/; the chat-move capability (8 requirements) is now baseline at orbit/specs/chat-move/spec.md.

judgements.reasoning: Both blind pairs were walked to closure and the system walk was verified landed. The tool has been run for real against both targets (home-env and home-env-test to the Mac mini, orbit-spec to the Fedora desktop) and resumed there, and the harness now exercises the remote shell boundary that the system pair found the gaps in.

accepted.claim: The real-machine re-run (task 5.6) was not performed; re-run no-op is established by the harness and by the home-env-test move leaving home-env's target chat unchanged.
accepted.why: The user declined re-running a live chat; the no-overwrite mechanism (rsync --ignore-existing) is the same on every run and is mutation-checked in the harness.

accepted.claim: The code-copy quoting assumes the source rsync is openrsync, which hands remote paths to the target shell unprotected; rsync 3.2.4+ on the source would double-escape names with spaces.
accepted.why: openrsync is the only rsync on the source's PATH; D6 names the assumption.

accepted.claim: Two moves to the same target at once are not coordinated on settings.json, and the in-place write is not atomic.
accepted.why: Moves are run by hand one at a time; the last writer still sets at least its own needed window; both trade-offs are in design Risks/D7.

accepted.claim: Scenario coverage is not registered in the scenario map.
accepted.why: The project's scenario check is off; coverage evidence lives in tasks 5.x and the harness.

next_recommended: /orbit:architect claude-chat-mover — change archived; review stage single-chat-move and take up the program's next stage, or run /orbit:audit-drift for a project-wide drift check.
